extracted.intended_audience: IB Diploma Programme mathematics teachers, IA assessors, and students preparing the Mathematics Internal Assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Rubric for assessing student Mathematics Internal Assessments (IAs) in the IB Diploma Programme, specifying five criteria (Presentation, Mathematical communication, Personal engagement, Reflection, Use of mathematics) with mark descriptors and HL/SL distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion A: Presentation (4 marks)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks descriptors: 0 — Does not reach the standards described below. 1 — Some coherence or organization. 2 — Some coherence and shows organization. 3 — Coherent and well organized. 4 — Coherent, well organized, concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion B: Mathematical communication (4 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses use of appropriate notation, symbols, terminology, and figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks descriptors: 0 — Does not reach the standard. 1 — Some relevant communication. 2 — Some appropriate notation; some clear definitions. 3 — Appropriate notation throughout; defined variables; key terms defined. 4 — Concise and precise notation; tables and graphs are well-labelled and self-explanatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion C: Personal engagement (3 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses extent to which the student takes ownership of the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks descriptors: 0 — None evidenced. 1 — Some personal engagement. 2 — Significant personal engagement. 3 — Outstanding personal engagement: independent thinking, creativity, presenting ideas in own way, exploring different perspectives, making and testing predictions. Note/anti-pattern: rote or copied textbook problems earn little or no personal engagement credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion D: Reflection (3 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses how the student reviews, analyses, and evaluates the exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks descriptors: 0 — None evidenced. 1 — Limited reflection. 2 — Meaningful reflection: evaluation of methods, discussion of limitations, comparison of approaches. 3 — Critical reflection: deeply insightful; evaluates results and implications; addresses limitations and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion E: Use of mathematics (6 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the mathematics produced (correctness, relevance, depth); separate SL and HL expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SL marks descriptors: 0 — None or off-topic. 1 — Some relevant mathematics, with errors. 2 — Relevant mathematics; some understanding. 3 — Relevant; mostly correct; partial demonstration of understanding. 4 — Relevant, correct, demonstrates understanding. 5 — Relevant, correct, demonstrates understanding, used precisely. 6 — Relevant, correct, precise, demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding. HL note: Same structure but additionally requires the mathematics to be at HL level (e.g., uses calculus / linear algebra / discrete-math beyond SL syllabus). Scoring note: a completely correct but rote computation is limited by personal engagement and may not reach highest E/C marks without originality and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: General expectations and distinctive features
rubrics_metrics.description: Overarching evaluative principles and common guidance emphasized by the rubric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Personal engagement is explicitly rewarded — originality, independent thinking, creativity and making/testing predictions increase marks; copying textbook problems is discouraged. 2) Reflection is required for top marks — doing the mathematics is necessary but evaluating meaning, limitations and implications is essential. 3) Communication (notation, labelling, clarity) is graded separately from correctness — a correct solution poorly presented can score poorly. 4) Presentation treats the IA as a written document (organization, concision) rather than a problem set. Influence note: rubric widely used in 150+ countries and resembles undergraduate research-paper rubrics; often used as model for high-school capstone math projects.
